newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine preliminary Feb fiscal deficit $420 mln.
newsitem.headline: Argentine preliminary Feb fiscal deficit $420 mln.

text.p: Preliminary estimates put Argentina's fiscal deficit for February at $420 million, compared to a $276 million gap in January and a $276 million shortfall in February 1996, Economy Ministry officials said Friday.
However, the February 1997 estimate includes the negative impact of the transfer of provincial pension funds to the central government, which was not included in the February 1996 measurement.
The broad fiscal number includes the accounts of central and decentralized state organisms, social security institutions and remaining public sector companies.
Argentina's stand-by agreement with the International Monetary Fund includes a $3.0 billion budget deficit target for 1997, or $4.5 billion including the provincial pension fund transfer.
The IMF-agreed target for the first quarter of the year is $1.04 billion, or $1.64 billion including the cost to central government of taking on loss-making provincial pension funds.

An Economy Ministry official who did not want to be named said an advance group of IMF officials would arrive in Buenos Aires in the first days of April to start checking the first quarter numbers. The official mission begins in late April.

The following month should see the start of negotiations for an IMF Extended Fund Facility the Argentine government hopes to have in place by the second half of this year, ready for when the stand-by loan agreement ends in December.
